## Design

### 2026-10-24 – I worked on making the schematic for the MIDI keypad. I wanted an OLED screen, an EC11 Rotary Encoder, the 7 touchpads, and 3 LEDs. I plan to have 3 modes: the 1st (main) mode acts like a MIDI keypad,

**3h**

I worked on making the schematic for the MIDI keypad. I wanted an OLED screen, an EC11 Rotary Encoder, the 7 touchpads, and 3 LEDs. I plan to have 3 modes: the 1st (main) mode acts like a MIDI keypad, the 2nd mode uses it as a general macro pad, and the 3rd mode is also a general macro pad but with different keybinds. I am using the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Zero as the microcontroller.

I started by adding the copper capacitive touch keys that use the electrical field generated by your body to detect if they are being touched. I just followed the guide and added the 7-pin generic connector
![InitiallyAddedTouchpadConnectors](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/30bf84e907d4415df64cac5ead70fb44394c35e5e081be4c44d376cd156b6899.png)

I then added the rotary encoder. I decided I wanted to use the switches to toggle through the different modes.

![RotaryEncoder](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/87df01976783b76d352fdabaa04d0fa1c1c58164aeaf8246a52024e1db989017.png)

Then I added the LEDs and chained 3 LEDs together to show which mode it is currently in, and any additional data to show for the MIDI part.

![LEDs](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/e54a714d73a54e8b729d9fa182411538b72259f46b4ac193bad0fcd600457873.png)

I then added the OLED to the RX and TX pins. I wired it directly because it was the last component and I didn't feel like using net labels.

I then ran the ERC, and it gave me 3 errors because KiCad did not know where the power was actually coming from.

![ErrorsOnERC](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/f5e7dd1e55f408838d9f40f007b760288bf70b44dad43cd72e16db7829d8779d.png)

I added PWR_FLAGs to the 3V3, 5V, and GND pins to show that these buses get power from the USB-C of the Waveshare ESP32.

![AddedPWR_FLAGS](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/9b6d14315a2eae7b97870d125f19a796b07f373cf953ac5473613f719666853d.png)

Then I ran the ERC again, and it showed no errors. The warnings are all because my grid is not a standard size.

![NoErrorsOnERC](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/8ae58a1c380e28332c65e068b1b63b9a66dd1b49634f780792798537ee167a6e.png)

Here is the finished schematic:

![EntireSchematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/1c59b658e3fa387d0d1ecd550e71293b3042fd8d14b6a7b3d55d0dde97186ddd.png)

### 2026-10-24 – I worked on creating the custom pads footprints, placing and laying out the PCB, and routing the PCB.

**4h**

I worked on creating the custom pads footprints, placing and laying out the PCB, and routing the PCB.

I followed the guide, and after the schematic, it says to create the footprint of the touch keys. I didn't like the piano design, so I created my own design to fit the hand, as if it were like a mouse, but with all 5 fingers, and 2 pads that need u to change which pad your thumb and index finger are on.

So pads 1 and 2 are for the thumb, with 2 being the resting button and 1 being the extended button.
Pads 3 and 4 are for the index finger, with 4 being the resting button and 3 being the extended button.
Pads 5, 6, and 7 are for the middle, ring, and pinky fingers in that order.

![CreatedCustomFootprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/caf0b91b7db0d3afde9e43905fccf2bcb9ef7a0860a742bbc8cb6e8827e5e7a6.png)

![NoWarningsFootprintChecker](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/49145e330c8026ca867be4ffc501d0a7c22408bc930c7626aa765c2917e2f314.png)

![AddedTouchFootprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/d02a7ece1355eb0ee931dee16bbd918071924b754a91347587bb64a3d0afd6ac.png)

This took the brunt of the time since I had never done this before; it was quite fun to do.

Next, I worked on the layout of the PCB. I wanted to make sure the whole thing was less than 100x100mm so that the cost would be lower, but my custom footprint was too big, so I shrunk down the pad sizes and locations to make it fit. Then I placed all the different components in such a way that it would fit.

![PCBLayoutDone](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/a70c927c783ded4d6cbf1522a4c515c7d3500cbc0bb0532acc475fac149840be.png)

I then routed the PCB. I also had to change some of the net labels on the schematic to make the routing neater. I think it turned out pretty good — only 2 vias and overall pretty neat I think. Here is the finished routing of the PCB:

![RoutedPCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/8e1d05775dc3974995ce8d4600b09ec2786a2acbaf30dcda01794251344bf4b9.png)

And the updated Pinout of the microcontroller (pretty much only the rotary encoder net labels changed):

![UpdatedSchematicESPPinout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/9d3544498f488f512df058803f5b7657a34750cc3e2fd71fe5a3d43f144647fe.png)

### 2026-10-24 – I did the GND fill for the board so that the GND isn't individually connected, but I had a lot of different errors from the DRC rule checker ( I wanted to work fast, so I didn't get a chance to screen

**1h**

I did the GND fill for the board so that the GND isn't individually connected, but I had a lot of different errors from the DRC rule checker ( I wanted to work fast, so I didn't get a chance to screenshot all of them).

The zone fill I initially did gave me 2 errors; one of them was just how the LEDs are, and I didn't realise for a while, but the guide says to just ignore those warnings. The second warning was that one of the GND pins didn't have 2 spokes; that also took me a while to solve.

![DRCBugs2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/783b46cc4271c22b70037afb72f34d407ac2d339fc29e4c4516d3ba43e2d3206.png)

![DRCBugs1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/d4b32b4197cc8b7133330940edf39315d20889c73620262839ccf44370d85f54.png)

Then I also realised there was a bug that showed that a DIN pin on one of the LEDs was disconnected and the LED bus was connected to the DOUT pin. This was an error in the schematic from when I changed the schematic to better match the physical layout, so I updated the schematic to fix this issue. Here is the old and updated schematic:
OLD:
![OldLEDSchematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/d61a181e9e250b126dc6bcb733425f13a862a201d51901b045da90531be33dde.png)

Updated:
![UpdatedLEDSchematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/85b8cca6f49b4b75835bd5ae57cdd528d5997021e843b389f13c612e3065e3b7.png)

I then deleted the original zone fill, rerouted the LEDs (had to flip them on the PCB itself as well), and then fixed one or 2 minor errors as well. The brunt of the time was figuring out which errors needed to be ignored and figuring out what was wrong with the LEDs.

Updated PCB:

![UpdatedZoneFillPCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/fc14860c2f3241d3bb3f60b30ecbdd366b17a367625c1848d0037c1539218e6f.png)

### 2026-10-25 – I worked on making and finalising the BOM and README.md.

**1h**

I worked on making and finalising the BOM and README.md.

I started by exporting all of the necessary KiCad files using the Fabricate plugin, then I moved on to finding the individual components for the BOM. I already have the rotary encoder, but everything else needs to be bought. It took me a while to find reliable but cheap components on AliExpress, and I also started off with getting all the values in CAD, so I had to find all of them again in USD, which took a while.
[Here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1wcF_mPrZf543xQacLG9ci4BRGrGUtqLDjnGJwcqraqM/edit?usp=sharing) is the finalised BOM as a Google spreadsheet (note the rotary encoder does not need to be bought, so the total falls under $30 USD).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/e1baf58f5a2a228db2d16c73bb71ca4d3b971da27fb2ce8acadc8950cf57e1f0.png)

I also finalised the README and added all the necessary information (I hope), learning from feedback on previous projects.
